defect: ViewLineMapping::contains_byte matches any row with no source bytes whenever byte_pos == self.line_end_byte, and CachedLayout::find_visual_row returns the first matching row. Because split_rendering.rs assigns line_end_byte = 0 to plugin-injected LineAbove virtual rows (which have all-None char_source_bytes), a virtual header above buffer line 1 claims byte 0; pressing Down from byte 0 resolves the cursor to row 0 (the header) and steps to row 1 (byte 0 again), stranding the cursor at the start of the buffer.
location: crates/fresh-editor/src/app/types.rs, ViewLineMapping::contains_byte and CachedLayout::find_visual_row / move_visual_line, lines 677-810
trigger: Open a buffer with line wrapping enabled and a LineAbove virtual line (such as a git-blame header) above line 1, place the cursor at byte 0, and press Down.
match_rule: Must identify that contains_byte / find_visual_row matches a virtual (all-None char_source_bytes) row at byte 0 via line_end_byte == 0, causing visual-line lookup or MoveDown from buffer start to resolve to the virtual header instead of the real line and strand the cursor.
near_misses: Complaining only about empty trailing EOF rows, wrapped line column clamping, or horizontal cursor movement.
why_findable: The diff adds contains_byte matching empty/virtual rows on byte_pos == line_end_byte and find_visual_row taking the first match; split_rendering.rs at intro already emits LineAbove virtual rows with all-None char_source_bytes and line_end_byte = 0.
notes: base = intro^; naive top_blamed was types.rs split refactor 5deddcac9, traced back to 57f3050055 which introduced contains_byte and move_visual_line.

defect: Editor::disable_lsp_for_buffer clears metadata.lsp_opened_with so re-enabling LSP will resend didOpen, but never sends textDocument/didClose or removes the path from LspState::document_versions. When LSP is toggled back on after edits, handle.did_open is silently dropped by should_skip_did_open in async_handler.rs because document_versions still contains the path, leaving the LSP server with stale content and causing desync on subsequent didChange deltas.
trigger: Open a file with LSP active, toggle LSP off for the buffer, edit the buffer, toggle LSP back on, and edit again.
match_rule: Must identify that disabling LSP clears lsp_opened_with without sending didClose (or clearing LspState::document_versions), so re-enabling LSP has its didOpen skipped by should_skip_did_open and desynchronizes the server.
near_misses: Complaining only about missing didSave, diagnostics clearing, or server shutdown when closing the editor.
why_findable: The diff adds disable_lsp_for_buffer clearing lsp_opened_with to re-trigger didOpen on re-enable, while async_handler.rs::should_skip_did_open in the repo at intro unconditionally skips didOpen whenever document_versions already holds the path.
notes: base = intro^; should_skip_did_open was already present since 7acbc6bca1 (2025-12-09).

defect: Editor::handle_replace_in_buffer saves the modified buffer directly with state.buffer.save_to_file(&path) without calling self.watch_file(&path) to refresh self.file_mod_times. On the next auto-revert poll, handle_file_changed sees the newer on-disk mtime as an external modification and invokes revert_buffer_by_id, which reloads from disk and resets the buffer's EventLog, wiping its undo history.
trigger: Run project-wide search & replace against an open buffer with auto-revert enabled, allow the file-change poller / handle_file_changed to tick, then attempt to Undo.
match_rule: Must identify that handle_replace_in_buffer calls save_to_file without refreshing watched mtime (watch_file / file_mod_times), causing auto-revert to treat the editor's own save as an external change and revert the buffer / wipe its event log.
near_misses: Complaining only about search-replace not recording a BulkEdit event, or file permission errors during save_to_file.
why_findable: The diff adds direct save_to_file in handle_replace_in_buffer without calling watch_file, whereas existing save paths in file_operations.rs call watch_file so poll_file_changes / handle_file_changed do not trigger revert_buffer_by_id.
notes: base = intro^; later commit 31f58d2aa added BulkEdit recording to handle_replace_in_buffer, exposing the pre-existing missing watch_file call introduced in 27b958181d.

defect: EventLog::is_at_saved_position now slices self.entries[start..end] where end can be saved_at_index, assuming saved_at_index <= self.entries.len(). However, EventLog::append truncates self.entries to self.current_index when appending after undo without invalidating saved_at_index, so saving, undoing, making a new edit, and calling is_at_saved_position panics with an out-of-bounds slice index.
location: src/model/event.rs, EventLog::is_at_saved_position, lines 554-573 (interacting with EventLog::append at line 650)
trigger: Make edits, call mark_saved(), undo past the save point, append a new edit (truncating entries below saved_at_index), and call is_at_saved_position().
match_rule: Must identify that is_at_saved_position slices self.entries up to saved_at_index while append() truncates self.entries without invalidating or clamping saved_at_index, causing an out-of-bounds panic.
near_misses: Complaining only about readonly event classification or reporting wrong dirty status when current_index == saved_at_index without mentioning the truncation/out-of-bounds slice.
why_findable: The diff introduces unchecked slicing self.entries[start..end] using saved_at_index, while EventLog::append in the same file clearly truncates self.entries without updating saved_at_index.
notes: base = intro^; before f2a22e0175, is_at_saved_position only compared saved_at_index == Some(current_index) and did not slice entries. Fix also added unit test crates/fresh-editor/src/model/event.rs::tests::test_is_at_saved_position_after_truncate.

defect: SplitRenderer collects linear selection_ranges from cursor.selection_range() for every cursor without excluding cursors in SelectionMode::Block, and then ORs selection_ranges with block_selections. Because BlockSelect actions set cursor.anchor alongside block_anchor and Cursor::selection_range() ignores selection_mode, every block selection is highlighted both as a full linear range across lines and as a 2D rectangle.
trigger: Create a multi-line rectangular block selection using Alt+Shift+Down and Alt+Shift+Right and render the viewport.
match_rule: Must identify that block-selection cursors still contribute to linear selection_ranges via cursor.selection_range() because SelectionMode::Block is not excluded, causing linear and rectangular selection highlights to both render.
near_misses: Complaining only about UTF-8 byte vs column coordinates, cursor exclusion from highlight, or multi-cursor overlap.
why_findable: The diff adds block_selections right after selection_ranges and ORs them together, while src/actions.rs (in the same diff) sets anchor during block selection and src/cursor.rs::selection_range() returns anchor..position regardless of selection_mode.
notes: base = intro^; naive top_blamed was 42a8e3ee38 (split_rendering extraction), traced back to fb42fec2d1 which introduced block selection rendering.

defect: restore_terminal_from_session switches session reload from replaying the raw log to loading the saved backing file directly via load_terminal_backing_file_as_buffer, but calls terminal_manager.spawn(..., Some(backing_path.clone())) and create_terminal_buffer_detached(terminal_id) beforehand. TerminalManager::spawn opens backing_path with truncate(true), and create_terminal_buffer_detached unconditionally writes an empty string to backing_file, erasing all saved scrollback before it can be loaded.
location: src/app/session.rs, Editor::restore_terminal_from_session, lines 477-545; src/services/terminal/manager.rs, TerminalManager::spawn, lines 221-230
trigger: Open a terminal, produce scrollback output, save the session, restart the editor, and restore the session.
match_rule: Must identify that session restore now relies on reading the existing backing file, yet spawn() (opening with truncate(true)) and/or create_terminal_buffer_detached (std::fs::write(..., "")) truncates/overwrites that backing file before load_terminal_backing_file_as_buffer reads it.
near_misses: Complaining only about save_session not flushing visible screen, log file rotation, or terminal resize.
why_findable: The diff both switches restore_terminal_from_session to load backing_path directly and passes backing_path into TerminalManager::spawn where the same diff opens it with .truncate(true); create_terminal_buffer_detached in src/app/terminal.rs also visibly overwrites backing_file with "".
notes: base = intro^; before 91601c7549, restore replayed the raw .log file and regenerated backing_file, so truncating backing_file did not lose scrollback.

defect: parse_osc7_path gates stripping the leading slash from file:///C:/... URIs behind #[cfg(windows)] and validates absoluteness via host-OS PathBuf::is_absolute(). On Windows, valid POSIX OSC 7 paths (such as /home/user/project from a remote/WSL shell or the module's own tests) fail is_absolute() and are rejected; on Unix, Windows file:///C:/... URIs from a remote shell retain the leading slash.
trigger: Process an OSC 7 sequence carrying a POSIX path on Windows (e.g. ESC ] 7 ; file://host/home/user BEL) or a Windows drive URI on Unix (ESC ] 7 ; file:///C:/Users/me/proj BEL).
match_rule: Must identify that parse_osc7_path uses host-OS-specific Path::is_absolute() (and/or #[cfg(windows)] drive-slash stripping), causing POSIX OSC 7 paths to be rejected on Windows or Windows drive URIs to be misparsed on non-Windows hosts.
near_misses: Complaining only about percent-decoding edge cases, hostname validation, or OSC 7 max payload length.
why_findable: Single function in the diff pairs #[cfg(windows)] stripping with PathBuf::is_absolute() while the same diff's unit tests pass POSIX paths (/...) that fail Path::is_absolute() on Windows.
notes: base = intro^; local single-site defect in parse_osc7_path (relation: false).

defect: SplitRenderer::render_composite_buffer takes an immutable &CompositeViewState and computes pane_widths into a local Vec without ever storing them back into view_state.pane_widths, which stays initialized to zeros (vec![0; pane_count]). Consumers in composite_buffer_actions.rs read view_state.pane_widths for horizontal scrolling and click hit-testing, so pane_width stays 0 and horizontal auto-scroll never engages (and clicks cannot map to non-zero panes).
trigger: Open a side-by-side composite diff view with a line wider than the pane and move the cursor right past the visible width (or click the right pane).
match_rule: Must identify that render_composite_buffer computes pane_widths locally without persisting them to CompositeViewState::pane_widths (which remains zeros), breaking downstream pane-width consumers such as horizontal scrolling or click hit-testing.
near_misses: Complaining only about gutter width constant 4, header height, or vertical scroll synchronization.
why_findable: The diff adds render_composite_buffer taking &CompositeViewState and computing local pane_widths while the same diff's handle_composite_click (and CompositeViewState::new initializing pane_widths to vec![0; pane_count]) reads view_state.pane_widths without any writer ever populating it.
notes: base = intro^; fix also synced horizontal scroll across all panes in composite_view.rs.

defect: EditorState stores LSP folding ranges as raw static line numbers in Vec<lsp_types::FoldingRange>, populated in async_messages.rs and queried directly by line number in split_rendering.rs, lsp_actions.rs, and input.rs, without backing them with MarkerList byte markers or shifting them on edits. Inserting or deleting lines before or inside a fold leaves fold gutter indicators and Toggle Fold misaligned on stale line numbers until the LSP happens to re-publish.
location: crates/fresh-editor/src/state.rs, EditorState::folding_ranges, line 163 (read in split_rendering.rs, lsp_actions.rs, input.rs)
trigger: Receive LSP folding ranges for a file, insert or delete a line above a foldable function, and inspect or click the fold gutter indicator on the function's new line.
match_rule: Must identify that LSP folding_ranges are stored as static line numbers without marker tracking or edit adjustment, so inserting/deleting lines causes fold indicators and fold toggling to drift onto the wrong lines.
near_misses: Complaining only about collapsed FoldManager ranges, workspace persistence of folds, or indent-based folding.
why_findable: The diff introduces Vec<FoldingRange> on EditorState alongside existing MarkerList-backed overlays/folds and queries raw start_line/end_line during rendering and fold toggle without any update path on buffer inserts/deletes.
notes: base = intro^; fix also updates test_fold_indicator_follows_delete_before_fold.

defect: In markdown_compose.ts, processLineConceals calls editor.clearOverlaysInRange(bufferId, byteStart, byteEnd) before rebuilding its own md-emphasis overlays. Because PluginCommand::ClearOverlaysInRange removes all overlays overlapping that range regardless of namespace, toggling or refreshing markdown compose mode erases editor-owned LSP diagnostic overlays (underline highlights, gutter dots, and E:N counts).
trigger: Open a Markdown file with an active LSP diagnostic (e.g. harper), then toggle Markdown Compose mode.
match_rule: Must identify that markdown_compose calls clearOverlaysInRange across all namespaces instead of scoping to its own overlay namespace, wiping editor-owned overlays such as LSP diagnostics.
near_misses: Complaining only about conceal clearing, table border alignment, or LSP diagnostic refresh debouncing.
why_findable: The diff adds editor.clearOverlaysInRange(bufferId, byteStart, byteEnd) in processLineConceals while the Rust plugin command handler / OverlayManager::remove_in_range in the repo at intro removes overlays across all namespaces including LSP diagnostics.
notes: base = intro^; verified 65c27755ca^ had no clearOverlaysInRange call in markdown_compose.ts.

defect: The AsyncMessage::LspServerQuiescent handler loops over all open buffers and sends an inlay_hints request for each, overwriting the single scalar self.pending_inlay_hints_request = Some(request_id) on every iteration. Because the AsyncMessage::LspInlayHints response handler drops any response whose request_id != self.pending_inlay_hints_request, only the last buffer's inlay hints are accepted and all other open buffers' responses are silently discarded as stale.
trigger: Open two or more buffers for the same LSP language, wait for experimental/serverStatus with quiescent=true, and observe inlay hints arriving for each buffer.
match_rule: Must identify that the LspServerQuiescent loop overwrites the single Option<u64> pending_inlay_hints_request on each buffer iteration, causing the LspInlayHints response guard to discard all earlier buffers' responses as stale.
near_misses: Complaining only about not filtering buffers by language, or inlay hints failing on a single buffer.
why_findable: The diff adds a multi-buffer loop writing self.pending_inlay_hints_request = Some(request_id) inside src/editor.rs right next to the existing LspInlayHints handler that rejects any request_id not matching that single Option.
notes: base = intro^; tiny 88-line diff introducing the multi-buffer quiescent re-request loop.

defect: The AsyncMessage::FileChanged handler updates file_last_revert_times and permanently disables self.auto_revert_enabled (and drops self.file_watcher) on any second event within 1 second BEFORE checking whether path is even open in any buffer (which only happens inside handle_file_changed). Because the watcher monitors entire parent directories, routine external saves (emitting multiple events or temp files like vim's 4913 in the watched directory) permanently disable auto-revert.
trigger: Open a file with auto-revert enabled and save it externally (or write a temp file twice within 1 second in the same watched directory).
match_rule: Must identify that rapid-change auto-disable triggers in AsyncMessage::FileChanged before filtering to open buffers (so unrelated files in watched directories trip it) and/or triggers permanently on just two events within 1s from a normal external save.
near_misses: Complaining only about the pre-flagged TODO comment on preserving cursor position across auto-revert.
why_findable: The diff moves debounce/auto-disable out of handle_file_changed (where open-buffer filtering lives) into AsyncMessage::FileChanged ahead of handle_file_changed, while watched_dirs in the same file watches whole directories.
notes: base = intro^; note that the diff contains a TODO comment about cursor preservation, which is a different issue — this entry is specifically for the auto-disable defect.

defect: This commit adds per-buffer toggles for Current Line Highlight (storing highlight_current_line_override on BufferViewState) and Occurrence Highlight (storing highlight_occurrences_override on BufferSettings and mutating state.reference_highlight_overlay.enabled), but never updates Editor::reset_buffer_settings. Running Reset Buffer Settings clears BufferSettings overrides without re-deriving reference_highlight_overlay.enabled or clearing BufferViewState::highlight_current_line_override, leaving both highlights stuck at their pinned state.
trigger: Pin Current Line Highlight or Occurrence Highlight for the current buffer via the per-buffer toggle, then run Reset Buffer Settings.
match_rule: Must identify that the new per-buffer highlight overrides are not cleared/re-derived by reset_buffer_settings (leaving reference_highlight_overlay.enabled and/or BufferViewState::highlight_current_line_override stuck after reset).
near_misses: Complaining only about command palette fuzzy ranking, status message translation text, or global toggle persistence.
why_findable: The diff adds two new per-buffer pin fields in toggle_actions.rs without updating reset_buffer_settings in the same file, which only calls clear_user_overrides() on BufferSettings.
notes: base = intro^; verified against bbedf2cb83 regression test.

defect: normalize_key unconditionally ORs KeyModifiers::SHIFT into modifiers whenever code is an ASCII uppercase KeyCode::Char. When CapsLock is active on terminals using the kitty keyboard protocol, Ctrl+A arrives as Char('A') + CONTROL (without SHIFT), and normalize_key turns it into Char('a') + CONTROL|SHIFT, breaking standard Ctrl+<letter> shortcuts.
trigger: Enable CapsLock in a terminal sending uppercase Char('A') with KeyModifiers::CONTROL (no SHIFT) and press Ctrl+A / Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V.
match_rule: Must identify that normalize_key unconditionally adds KeyModifiers::SHIFT for uppercase ASCII Char events, turning CapsLock-modified shortcuts (uppercase Char without SHIFT) into Shift-modified chords that fail to match Ctrl+<letter> bindings.
near_misses: Complaining only about BackTab shift stripping, non-ASCII Unicode letters, or mode inheritance removal.
why_findable: normalize_key is added in the diff and visibly synthesizes KeyModifiers::SHIFT from c.is_ascii_uppercase() even when SHIFT is not set in modifiers.
notes: base = intro^; local single-function defect in normalize_key (relation: false).

defect: Editor::toggle_comment switches from calling detect_language(path, &self.config.languages) to reading self.active_state().language, while EditorState::from_file_with_languages initializes state.language solely from tree-sitter's Language::from_path(path) and falls back to "text". Configured languages without a tree-sitter grammar (such as YAML/YML, which have comment_prefix configured in config.rs) now get language = "text", breaking toggle_comment.
location: src/state.rs, EditorState::from_file / from_file_with_languages, lines 229-236 and 306-314; src/app/render.rs, Editor::toggle_comment, lines 2878-2885
trigger: Open a .yaml or .yml file and invoke Toggle Comment (Ctrl+/).
match_rule: Must identify that toggle_comment now relies on EditorState::language, which is populated only via tree-sitter Language::from_path (falling back to "text") instead of config-based detect_language, breaking languages configured in config.languages without tree-sitter support (such as YAML).
near_misses: Complaining only about comment prefix trailing spaces, multi-cursor commenting, or Save As language re-detection.
why_findable: The diff changes toggle_comment from detect_language(path, &self.config.languages) to state.language while setting state.language in src/state.rs only from Language::from_path (even though from_file_with_languages already takes languages and config.rs defines yaml/etc. absent from Language::from_path).
notes: base = intro^; fix also added test_toggle_comment_yml_prefix.

defect: SettingsState::tree_cursor_index and render_categories derive the categories-panel cursor from current_section_index() (which tracks the body's topmost visible item). Expanding a category with Right immediately snaps selection to section 0, and pressing Down calls tree_step -> ensure_visible(), which scrolls minimally so topmost_visible_item_index stays in section 0, causing tree_cursor_index to return section 0 again and trapping Down navigation.
location: crates/fresh-editor/src/view/settings/state.rs, SettingsState::tree_step and tree_cursor_index, lines 346-428; crates/fresh-editor/src/view/settings/render.rs, render_categories, lines 532-540
trigger: Open Settings, expand a multi-section category with Right, and press Down to step through its child sections.
match_rule: Must identify that deriving the tree cursor from current_section_index() / body topmost visible item causes Right-expand to jump off the category row and/or Down navigation to get stuck because minimal scrolling (ensure_visible) leaves topmost_visible_item_index on the first section.
near_misses: Complaining only about auto-expand on click, mouse-wheel scrolling, or category highlight colors.
why_findable: The diff changes tree_cursor_index to prioritize current_section_index() and calls ensure_visible() in tree_step, while current_section_index() and ScrollablePanel::ensure_focused_visible in the repo at intro only scroll minimally to keep selected_item in view rather than moving it to the top.
notes: base = intro^; fix added 6 e2e tests including right_to_expand_does_not_jump_cursor_to_first_section and down_after_expand_walks_into_first_section.

defect: SuggestionsRenderer::render_with_hover returns only inner_area into cached_layout.suggestions_area, and handle_mouse_click only hit-tests that inner item rect (and likewise ignores the outer rect in popup_areas). Clicks on the suggestions popup's outer border or non-item chrome rows are not absorbed as popup clicks and fall through to the underlying editor split, moving the buffer cursor.
location: src/ui/suggestions.rs, SuggestionsRenderer::render_with_hover, lines 39-149; src/editor.rs, suggestions_area hit-testing, lines 5384-5560
trigger: Open a prompt with a suggestions popup (such as Command Palette or Reload with Encoding) and click on the popup's border or empty padding row.
match_rule: Must identify that only the suggestions popup's inner item rect is cached/checked for mouse clicks, so clicks on the popup's outer border/chrome fall through to the underlying editor buffer instead of being absorbed.
near_misses: Complaining only about hover highlighting, item index math inside inner_area, or single-click vs double-click confirmation.
why_findable: The diff introduces cached_layout.suggestions_area storing only inner_area returned by SuggestionsRenderer::render_with_hover (and leaves _popup_rect unused in popup_areas hit-testing), so handle_mouse_click only consumes clicks inside inner_rect and lets border/chrome clicks fall through to split click handling.
notes: base = intro^; fix also added double-click confirm for preview-on-click prompts.

defect: Handling PluginCommand::ShowActionPopup pushes each popup onto the PopupManager stack via self.show_popup(popup) while storing action-popup tracking in a single scalar self.active_action_popup: Option<(String, Vec<(String, String)>)>. When a second plugin calls showActionPopup while a first action popup is still open, it overwrites self.active_action_popup; after dismissing the top popup (which calls take()), the underlying first popup has no tracking entry and never fires its action_popup_result hook.
location: src/app/mod.rs, Editor::active_action_popup and PluginCommand::ShowActionPopup handler, lines 508 and 3764; src/app/popup_actions.rs, lines 20-55
trigger: Have two plugins call showActionPopup concurrently, dismiss or confirm the top popup, then dismiss or confirm the first popup underneath.
match_rule: Must identify that PopupManager stacks multiple popups while active_action_popup is a single Option that gets overwritten by a second showActionPopup, causing the first popup to lose its tracking/callback (action_popup_result) once the top popup is resolved.
near_misses: Complaining only about popup positioning across buffer switches, status message overwrite, or single-popup dismissal.
why_findable: The diff adds self.active_action_popup: Option<...> overwritten on every ShowActionPopup and consumed via take() in popup_actions.rs, while PopupManager::show in the repo at intro pushes onto a stack (Vec<Popup>) rather than replacing.
notes: base = intro^; fix also added action_popups_queue_confirms_preserve_per_popup_identity.

defect: Editor::extract_terminal_tab_to_new_workspace calls create_window_at(root, label), immediately moves the live PTY handle and terminal buffer into target, and then calls set_active_window(target) without materializing target first. When target reuses an existing dormant (pending-restore) session for that root, set_active_window's lazy materialize_window rebuilds the window wholesale via Window::from_workspace, discarding the just-adopted live PTY and buffer.
trigger: Have a dormant (unmaterialized) persisted workspace for directory D, cd a live terminal in another workspace to D, and run Extract Tab to New Workspace.
match_rule: Must identify that extract_terminal_tab_to_new_workspace moves the terminal/buffer into the window returned by create_window_at before materializing it, so set_active_window's lazy materialization overwrites the window and discards the moved live PTY/buffer.
near_misses: Complaining only about PTY output tag remapping, remote dormant shells, or source-window leaf retargeting.
why_findable: The diff calls create_window_at -> move_terminal_machinery_to_window -> set_active_window in window_actions.rs, where create_window_at returns an existing unmaterialized window for that root and set_active_window lazily runs materialize_window (rebuilding Window::from_workspace).
notes: base = intro^; a8a2e56239 introduced the same pattern for file tabs and 6029b8f71 introduced extract_terminal_tab_to_new_workspace directly tested by extract_terminal_into_dormant_session_keeps_live_pty.

defect: handle_attach_remote_agent parses EksTarget (including target.workspace) and connects to the remote EKS pod, but sends AsyncMessage::RemoteAttachReady without the pod workspace path and calls install_authority_with_keepalive -> install_authority -> request_restart(self.working_dir.clone()). After attaching, the editor restarts with the pod's remote filesystem rooted at the stale local host path, breaking file open, quick-open, and file explorer.
trigger: Call attachRemoteAgent for an EKS target whose pod workspace (e.g. /workspace) differs from the local editor's working directory, then browse or open files.
match_rule: Must identify that attachRemoteAgent / install_authority_with_keepalive drops EksTarget.workspace and restarts the editor at the local working_dir instead of the remote pod workspace, causing remote filesystem operations to run against a local host path.
near_misses: Complaining only about keepalive lifetime, kubectl RBAC preflight, or SSH startup path handling.
why_findable: The diff parses target.workspace on EksTarget, wires RemoteAttachReady to install_authority_with_keepalive, and delegates directly to install_authority which calls self.request_restart(self.working_dir.clone()) with the local directory.
notes: base = intro^; fix updated the existing test to assert the restart re-roots at /workspace.

defect: In TabsRenderer::render_for_split, the loop over split_buffers skips any buffer ID missing from the buffers HashMap before pushing to tab_ranges, so tab_ranges can be shorter than split_buffers. However, active_tab_idx is computed via split_buffers.iter().position(...) and then used to index tab_ranges[active_tab_idx] directly, panicking with index out of bounds whenever a stale/missing buffer ID precedes the active buffer.
trigger: Render a split's tab bar when split_buffers contains a stale buffer ID absent from buffers before the active buffer (such as closing and reopening keyboard shortcuts help).
match_rule: Must identify that active_tab_idx is computed as an index into split_buffers while tab_ranges omits entries skipped via buffers.get(id) == None, causing tab_ranges[active_tab_idx] to panic or address the wrong tab.
near_misses: Complaining only about scroll indicator width arithmetic, tab truncation, or compute_tab_scroll_offset clamping.
why_findable: Within TabsRenderer::render_for_split, the diff computes active_tab_idx from split_buffers and indexes tab_ranges[active_tab_idx] right below the loop that continues when buffers.get(id) is None.
notes: base = intro^; single-function index mismatch in TabsRenderer::render_for_split (relation: false).

defect: Editor::handle_rename_response applies a multi-file LSP WorkspaceEdit by calling self.open_file(&path) for every URI in workspace_edit.changes without saving and restoring the originally active buffer. Because open_file unconditionally switches active_buffer and the active split to the opened file, a cross-file rename yanks focus away from the invoking buffer to whichever other file was iterated last in the HashMap.
trigger: Invoke LSP rename (F2) from a use site in file A on a symbol defined in file B so the WorkspaceEdit touches both files.
match_rule: Must identify that applying WorkspaceEdit calls open_file() for each touched URI without restoring the original active buffer, causing cross-file rename to steal focus away from the buffer where rename was invoked.
near_misses: Complaining only about edit sort order within a file, UTF-16 position conversion, or unsaved changes in other files.
why_findable: The diff adds handle_rename_response looping over workspace_edit.changes and calling self.open_file(&path), while Editor::open_file in the same file visibly sets self.active_buffer and updates split_manager to focus the opened buffer.
notes: base = intro^; naive top_blamed was 7d919b20a6 (extract lsp_requests.rs), traced back to b704976e3.

defect:
TextEdit::value joins self.lines with '
' (representing a trailing newline as a trailing empty element, e.g. ["a", ""] -> "a
"), but TextEdit::set_value populates self.lines with text.lines().map(String::from).collect(). Because Rust's str::lines() strips a final trailing newline, set_value("a
") yields ["a"] and silently deletes trailing newlines on round-trips (including undo/redo snapshot restoration).
location: src/view/ui/text_edit.rs, TextEdit::set_value, lines 92-104 (paired with TextEdit::value at line 87)
trigger: Call TextEdit::set_value("a\n") on a multiline TextEdit (or type 'a', Enter, 'b' and undo once) and read value().
match_rule: Must identify that TextEdit::set_value uses str::lines(), which drops a trailing empty line/newline and disagrees with value() joining lines with '\n'.
near_misses: Complaining only about single-line mode, cursor clamping, or selection clearing in set_value.
why_findable: value() and set_value() sit five lines apart in the diff; value() uses join("\n") while set_value() uses text.lines(), which by Rust stdlib contract omits a trailing empty line after a final '\n'.
notes: base = intro^; local single-struct defect between adjacent value() and set_value() methods (relation: false). Fix also added test_undo_restores_trailing_newline.

defect: This commit adds a guard in Editor::set_active_window to clear the outgoing window's panel-scoped editor_mode whenever self.floating_widget_panel.is_some(), so switching away while a floating panel is mounted does not strand the source window in that mode. However, Editor::create_window_with_terminal in the same file switches self.active_window = id directly without calling set_active_window or clearing previous_id's editor_mode, leaving the source window stuck in the panel's mode and swallowing all keyboard input when switched back to.
location: crates/fresh-editor/src/app/window_actions.rs, Editor::set_active_window, lines 284-315 (missing sibling path Editor::create_window_with_terminal at lines 145-210)
trigger: Open a floating panel that sets an editor_mode on window A (e.g. Orchestrator New-Session form), trigger create_window_with_terminal (born-attached remote session) before closing the form, then switch back to window A and type in a buffer.
match_rule: Must identify that clearing floating-panel-scoped editor_mode was added only to set_active_window while create_window_with_terminal also mutates self.active_window directly, leaving the source window's editor_mode stuck.
near_misses: Complaining only about persistent vi-mode being cleared, terminal_mode flags, or spawn rollback on error.
why_findable: The diff places the panel-mode cleanup exclusively in set_active_window in window_actions.rs, while create_window_with_terminal ~130 lines above in the same file visibly assigns self.active_window = id directly.
notes: base = intro^; verified create_window_with_terminal existed at line 145 of window_actions.rs at 36faa74890.

defect: SplitRenderer::render_content paints the split close button "×" at layout.tabs_rect.x + layout.tabs_rect.width - 2 on top of the tab bar after TabsRenderer::render_for_split has already rendered across the full layout.tabs_rect width. Because TabsRenderer draws the right-overflow scroll indicator ">" at the right edge of tabs_rect without reserving columns for the split button, the button overwrites the right-overflow indicator (and tab content under it).
trigger: Open multiple splits and enough tabs in one split to overflow the tab bar horizontally; inspect the right edge of the tab bar.
match_rule: Must identify that the split close button is rendered over the right edge of layout.tabs_rect without shrinking the width passed to TabsRenderer::render_for_split, overwriting the right tab-overflow indicator or rightmost tab.
near_misses: Complaining only about button hover color, file explorer close button, or tab name elision width.
why_findable: The diff renders close_button directly inside layout.tabs_rect at width - 2 right after calling TabsRenderer::render_for_split with the full layout.tabs_rect, while TabsRenderer in src/view/ui/tabs.rs at intro draws SCROLL_INDICATOR_RIGHT at the right edge of that same rect.
notes: base = intro^; verified tab scrolling (d83f09b44) predated 1cc9a762c9. Fix also added split_control_reserve_matches_button_count and updated crates/fresh-editor/tests/semantic/migrated_tab_scrolling.rs.

defect: TerminalManager::spawn infers session restore solely by checking whether backing_path already exists and is non-empty (existing_has_content), and create_terminal_buffer_detached skips truncating whenever backing_file exists. Because terminal IDs reset to 0 on each launch while backing files (fresh-terminal-<id>.txt) persist on disk and restored terminals keep their saved filename under a newly assigned ID, opening a brand-new terminal can collide with a restored terminal's active transcript or a leftover file from a previous run and inherit its scrollback.
location: src/services/terminal/manager.rs, TerminalManager::spawn, lines 231-255; src/app/terminal.rs, create_terminal_buffer_detached, lines 197-205
trigger: Create two terminals (ids 0 and 1), close terminal 0, save and restart (restoring fresh-terminal-1.txt under id 0), then open a new terminal (assigned id 1 -> fresh-terminal-1.txt); or leave a leftover fresh-terminal-0.txt from a prior run and open a new terminal.
match_rule: Must identify that inferring restore from existing non-empty backing file on disk (instead of explicit fresh vs restore intent and/or avoiding path collision with reset terminal IDs) causes a new terminal to share or inherit another/previous terminal's scrollback backing file.
near_misses: Complaining only about raw PTY log rotation, terminal buffer read-only flag, or restored terminal key_context.
why_findable: The diff introduces existing_has_content in TerminalManager::spawn (not distinguishing new vs restored terminals) while TerminalManager::next_terminal_id starts at 0 per process and src/app/terminal.rs / session.rs construct fresh-terminal-<id>.txt paths in a persistent directory.
notes: base = intro^; 2nd (and max) commit in the terminal-scrollback series (after 91601c7549 at order_index 10). Fix also added new_terminal_does_not_adopt_a_restored_terminal_transcript and new_terminal_discards_a_leftover_transcript_on_its_path.

defect: Auto-resuming terminal mode via terminal_mode_resume is wired exclusively inside Editor::set_active_buffer. Split focus transitions that change the active buffer via SplitManager without calling set_active_buffer—such as handle_close_split (closing a second split so focus returns to a terminal split) and next_split/prev_split—never record or consult terminal_mode_resume, leaving a previously live terminal stuck in read-only scrollback mode when it regains focus.
location: src/app/mod.rs, Editor::set_active_buffer, lines 2520-2538 (bypassed by next_split/prev_split at line 2104 and handle_close_split in src/app/plugin_commands.rs line 444)
trigger: Open a terminal in split 1 (live terminal mode), open a second split, exit/close the second split so focus collapses back to split 1, and type into the idle terminal.
match_rule: Must identify that terminal_mode_resume is only updated/checked in set_active_buffer and is bypassed by split-switching or split-closing focus paths (next_split/prev_split/handle_close_split), leaving a re-focused terminal out of terminal mode.
near_misses: Complaining only about explicit Ctrl+] TerminalEscape clearing, terminal process exit handling, or jump_to_end_on_output.
why_findable: The diff places all terminal_mode_resume insert/check logic solely in Editor::set_active_buffer, while next_split, prev_split (in the same file) and handle_close_split (in plugin_commands.rs) visibly change the active split/buffer directly via split_manager without invoking set_active_buffer.
notes: base = intro^; fix also added first_terminal_stays_in_scrollback_after_closing_second_split.

defect: Adding the Keybinding Editor modal wires key dispatch into dispatch_modal_input in input_dispatch.rs, but omits self.keybinding_editor.is_some() from the in_modal guard in dispatch_terminal_input right above it in the same file. When the Keybinding Editor is opened while a terminal buffer is in terminal mode, dispatch_terminal_input intercepts all keystrokes and sends them to the PTY instead of the modal.
trigger: Enter live terminal mode in an embedded terminal, open the Keybinding Editor modal, and press navigation or search keys.
match_rule: Must identify that self.keybinding_editor.is_some() is missing from the in_modal guard in dispatch_terminal_input, so terminal mode grabs keystrokes and forwards them to the PTY while the Keybinding Editor modal is open.
near_misses: Complaining only about focus highlight colors in the edit dialog, Tab button cycling, or non-terminal modal dispatch order.
why_findable: The diff edits crates/fresh-editor/src/app/input_dispatch.rs to dispatch keybinding_editor right next to calibration_wizard, while lines 24-28 of the same file explicitly list every modal (including calibration_wizard) in dispatch_terminal_input's in_modal guard.
notes: base = intro^; verified lines 24-28 of input_dispatch.rs at 53c2e09b4a.

defect: Editor::render calls self.animations.capture_before_all(frame.buffer_mut()) at the start of the render pass so SlideIn can snapshot the previous frame's cells for push transitions. However, ratatui's Terminal::draw clears/resets the current buffer on swap_buffers before invoking the render closure, so frame.buffer_mut() is always blank at the top of render and push transitions capture empty cells instead of pushing out the previous frame.
location: crates/fresh-editor/src/app/render.rs, Editor::render, line 13; crates/fresh-editor/src/view/animation.rs, AnimationRunner::capture_before_all and SlideIn::capture_before, lines 56-135
trigger: Render a frame with content, then start a SlideIn push animation on the next ratatui Terminal::draw frame and observe mid-transition cells.
match_rule: Must identify that calling capture_before_all(frame.buffer_mut()) at the start of Editor::render samples a blank/reset buffer because ratatui clears the active draw buffer before each frame, so push transitions capture blank cells instead of the previous frame.
near_misses: Complaining only about mid-animation terminal resize handling, easing math, or animation duration.
why_findable: The diff calls capture_before_all(frame.buffer_mut()) at the start of Editor::render assuming the frame buffer contains the prior frame, whereas ratatui::Terminal::draw (used across main.rs and tests in the repo) resets the current buffer before every render callback.
notes: base = intro^; 25th distinct admitted relation:true diff (stop_index = 57).

defect: `aa792bd4ce` wires `highlight_current_line` from `editor.highlight_current_line` config and `ToggleCurrentLineHighlight` through `BufferViewState` into `ViewPreferences::highlight_current_line`, and passes it in layout-only computation, but `SplitRenderer::render_buffer_in_split` omits the parameter and hardcodes `true, // highlight_current_line` when calling `Self::compute_buffer_layout`. Disabling `editor.highlight_current_line` in config or toggling it off via the command palette has no effect on rendered output.
trigger: Configure `editor.highlight_current_line: false` (or run `Toggle Current Line Highlight` to turn it off) and render an active buffer split.
match_rule: Must identify that `render_buffer_in_split` hardcodes `true` for `highlight_current_line` when calling `compute_buffer_layout` instead of accepting and forwarding `view_prefs.highlight_current_line` from `render_split` / `BufferViewState`.
near_misses: Complaining only about the highlight not spanning trailing empty columns or missing locale translations without identifying the hardcoded `true` ignoring `view_prefs.highlight_current_line`.
why_findable: The diff adds `ViewPreferences::highlight_current_line` populated from `view_state.highlight_current_line` and passes `view_prefs.highlight_current_line` to the layout-only call, while the actual rendering path `render_buffer_in_split` passes hardcoded `true` to `compute_buffer_layout`.
notes: base = intro^.

defect: When mapping a mouse column in grid-wrapped terminal scrollback to a buffer byte offset, `terminal_mouse.rs` calls `r.source_byte_at_visual_col(grid_col).unwrap_or(trimmed.len())`, assuming `source_byte_at_visual_col` returns `None` when `grid_col` is past the row's rendered content. However, `ViewLine::source_byte_at_visual_col` (`crates/fresh-editor/src/view/ui/view_pipeline.rs:85-97`) delegates to `char_at_visual_col`, which clamps out-of-range columns to `char_source_bytes.len().saturating_sub(1)` (the start byte of the last character) and returns `Some(...)`. Thus `.unwrap_or(trimmed.len())` is dead code on non-empty rows, and dragging past the end of a line drops its final character from the selection.
trigger: Enter terminal scrollback mode and drag-select across a line, releasing the mouse in empty cells past the end of the line's text.
match_rule: Must connect `terminal_mouse.rs` calling `r.source_byte_at_visual_col(grid_col).unwrap_or(trimmed.len())` to `ViewLine::source_byte_at_visual_col` / `char_at_visual_col` clamping out-of-range visual columns to the last character's start byte instead of returning `None` (or end-of-line), dropping the final character on overshoot.
near_misses: Complaining about ANSI escape width or tab expansion without identifying `source_byte_at_visual_col` clamping past-content columns to the last character's start byte.
why_findable: Inspecting the callee `ViewLine::source_byte_at_visual_col` -> `char_at_visual_col` in `crates/fresh-editor/src/view/ui/view_pipeline.rs:85-97` immediately shows `.unwrap_or_else(|| self.char_source_bytes.len().saturating_sub(1))`, so any `grid_col >= visual_width()` resolves to the start byte of the final character rather than `None`.
notes: base = intro^. Distinct feature (grid-wrap mouse selection in 2026-07) from the 2025-12 terminal scrollback persistence series.

defect:
The indentation-guide staircase scanner in `render_line/mod.rs:230` was refactored to call `indent_folding::slice_indent(line.text.as_bytes(), tab_size)` on `ViewLine::text`, which retains its trailing `'
'`. However, `indent_folding::slice_indent` in `crates/fresh-editor/src/view/folding.rs:441-462` requires a slice with no trailing `'
'` and matches only `b' '`, `b'	'`, and `b''`, treating `b'
'` via the `_` arm as non-whitespace content (`all_blank = false`, `indent = 0`). Every blank interior line (`"
"`) is misread as an indent-0 content line, popping the ancestor staircase and collapsing inner indentation guides on subsequent lines.
trigger: Open a file with indentation guides enabled (`all` mode) containing a blank line inside a nested indented block (e.g. an empty line between two indented statements).
match_rule: Must connect `render_line/mod.rs` passing newline-terminated `ViewLine::text` (`line.text.as_bytes()`) to `indent_folding::slice_indent` (`folding.rs`) treating `b'\n'` as non-whitespace content (`all_blank = false`, `indent = 0`), causing blank lines to collapse the indentation-guide staircase.
near_misses: Complaining about tab width calculation or soft-wrap continuation rows without identifying the `b'\n'` contract mismatch between `ViewLine::text` and `indent_folding::slice_indent`.
why_findable:
The diff replaces a bespoke helper in `render_line/mod.rs` with `indent_folding::slice_indent(line.text.as_bytes(), tab_size)`. Reading `indent_folding::slice_indent` in `crates/fresh-editor/src/view/folding.rs:435-462` explicitly states `(no trailing '
')` and sets `all_blank = false` on `b'
'`, whereas `ViewLine::text` preserves trailing `'
'`.
notes: base = intro^.

defect: `6aa901634a` introduces `Viewport::top_view_line_offset` (set by `ensure_visible_in_layout` and consumed during rendering to skip leading view lines starting at `top_byte`), but `Viewport::ensure_visible` (and `set_top_byte_with_limit`) updates `self.top_byte` to a new line without resetting `self.top_view_line_offset = 0`. Once `top_view_line_offset` becomes non-zero, subsequent `ensure_visible` scrolls jump `top_byte` while leaving the stale offset intact, causing rendering to skip extra view lines below the new `top_byte`.
location: src/viewport.rs, Viewport::top_view_line_offset (line 18), ensure_visible_in_layout (line 245), and ensure_visible / set_top_byte_with_limit (lines 303-665)
trigger: Scroll into a buffer state with a non-zero `top_view_line_offset` (e.g., wrapped or virtual lines at the top of the viewport) and then move the cursor so `Viewport::ensure_visible` scrolls to a new `top_byte`.
match_rule: Must identify that `Viewport::ensure_visible` (or `set_top_byte_with_limit`) changes `self.top_byte` without resetting `self.top_view_line_offset` to `0`, leaving a stale view-line offset that shifts rendering after scrolling.
near_misses: Complaining only about `scroll_view_lines` clamping or horizontal `left_column` without identifying the stale `top_view_line_offset` when `ensure_visible` updates `top_byte`.
why_findable: The diff adds `top_view_line_offset` to `Viewport`, mutates it in `ensure_visible_in_layout`, and skips `top_view_line_offset` lines from `top_byte` during rendering, yet none of the `top_byte` mutation paths in `ensure_visible` / `set_top_byte_with_limit` reset `top_view_line_offset` to `0`.
notes: base = intro^; naive top_blamed was e3674284c5 (2025-11-15), which predated top_view_line_offset; traced via git log -S top_view_line_offset to 6aa901634a.

defect: When opening a nested dialog for an `ObjectArray` (or nested `Map`) field inside a map entry dialog, `SettingsState::open_nested_entry_dialog` constructs the child path as `format!("{}/{}", dialog.map_path, item.path.trim_start_matches('/'))`, omitting `dialog.entry_key`. When `save_array_item_dialog_inner` later calls `self.set_pending_change(&array_path, array_value)`, the JSON pointer lacks the outer map entry's key (e.g. `"/map_path/field"` instead of `"/map_path/<entry_key>/field"`), corrupting pending config changes by writing under the wrong path.
trigger: Open a Map entry dialog in the Settings UI whose value contains a nested `ObjectArray` (or nested `Map`) field, open the nested array-item dialog for that field, and save.
match_rule: Must connect `open_nested_entry_dialog` building `path` from `dialog.map_path` and `item.path` without including `dialog.entry_key` to saving pending changes (e.g. in `save_array_item_dialog_inner` -> `set_pending_change`) under a corrupted JSON pointer missing the outer map key.
near_misses: Complaining only about `quicklsp`'s `only_features` default (separate config change in the same fix) or `delete_entry_dialog` without identifying `open_nested_entry_dialog` omitting `dialog.entry_key`.
why_findable: In the same file `src/view/settings/state.rs`, `delete_entry_dialog` (line 867) joins `format!("{}/{}", dialog.map_path, dialog.entry_key)`, whereas `open_nested_entry_dialog` (line 677) joins `dialog.map_path` directly with `item.path`, dropping `dialog.entry_key`, and `save_array_item_dialog_inner` (line 856) passes that truncated `dialog.map_path` straight to `set_pending_change`.
notes: base = intro^; traced via git log -S open_nested_entry_dialog to 2fadc190b3.
